items.title: What the RSS didn’t tell its New York guests | Let Me Explain 161 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: We all saw the images from Madison Square Garden. Thousands of people. Aarti. A packed hall. And RSS Sarsangchalak Mohan Bhagwat at the centre of it all. On the surface, it looked like a big success for the RSS. But there was a problem. Some of the religious leaders invited to events around Bhagwat’s visit say they did not know what they were being invited to. And who they were being invited to stand alongside. And the emails we reviewed suggest the same thing. These leaders were invited to what was presented as an interfaith gathering called One World, One Humanity. Absolutely no mention of the RSS The guest of honor slot was left empty. Watch the full episode as I take you through these e mails. And also explain an important point- What exactly is the Sangh trying to build outside India? And why did its big international showcase raise so many questions? Let me explain. On August 29, Mohan Bhagwat addressed around 5,000 people at Madison Square Garden at the Universal Oneness Celebration. The event presented a very particular image of the RSS – religious unity, diversity and harmony. But earlier that day, several religious leaders had been invited to an event at the Pierre Hotel.

State of Karnataka]. A bench of Justice D K Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan said that Court's constitutional jurisdiction cannot be invoked repeatedly to unsettle an appointment in the absence of a clear legal infirmity. "The dignity of the office and the sanctity of the judicial process demand that both the office-holder and those who invoke the jurisdiction of the Court act with restraint, bona fides and fidelity to law," it added. Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan The Court said the petitioner had not been able to demonstrate that Vidyashankar suffers from any statutory disqualification which could render him ineligible to hold the office of Vice-Chancellor. "There is equally no material of such a nature as would establish that the appointment was made by an authority lacking jurisdiction or in patent violation of a mandatory statutory requirement," it added. items.title: Advocate not above the law: J&K High Court on lawyer's plea against police request for assistance
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh recently observed that merely being an advocate does not place a person above the law and that, as an officer of the court, a lawyer is expected to render lawful assistance to an investigating agency when required [Wasim Ahmed Reshi V/s UT of JK and others]. At the same time, the High Court cautioned the police that they are equally bound to act strictly in accordance with law and directed the investigating agency to scrupulously follow the prescribed procedure whenever it seeks the presence or assistance of an advocate during an investigation. “Merely because the petitioner is an advocate does not place him above the law. Rather, being an officer of the court and well versed with the legal position, he is expected to render such lawful assistance to the investigating agency as may be required so that the truth concerning the alleged offence is brought to light and, if an offence has indeed been committed, the offender is brought to justice. Such cooperation is in consonance with the administration of justice and the duties expected of an officer of the Court,” the High Court said. items.title: Law, music and cinema not strangers to each other: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana at NUALS seminar
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks. Drawing a parallel between music and law, the judge said that while music has rules, rhythm structure and harmony which help an artist create music, so does law which has Constitution, legislation and procedure which provides a framework within which judges and lawyers work. " Law is not entirely different, the Constitution, legislation and procedure give us our framework, they tell us where the boundaries are and so judges are constantly trying to do something quite delicate; to interpret law faithfully while recognising that the world in which the law operates is constantly changing. The answer to why art matters to law is rather simple. We spend a great deal of time in law dealing with categories, principles and procedures. But behind every case is a person, behind every legal dispute is a human experience, " Justice Mohana said. She was speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the ' Three-day Seminar on Music, Cinema and Law: Exploring the Intersections of Art, Culture and Law

items.title: Regulating arbitrators like Supreme Court, High Court judges is impossible: Retired Justice AK Sikri
items.summary: It would be impossible to regulate arbitrators in exactly the same manner as Supreme Court and High Court judges, former Supreme Court Justice AK Sikri said during a debate at India ADR Week 2026. Justice Sikri was one of the judges for the Oxford-style debate on whether arbitrators should be professionally regulated like judges. Judging the debate along him were Dentons Link Legal Managing Partner Atul Sharma and Carsten van de Sande of Hengeler Mueller. The debate was moderated by Saraf & Partners partner Sanya Sud . Justice Sikri said that the proposition itself could be understood in two ways: either that arbitrators should be subject to some form of regulation similar to judges, or that they should be regulated through the same mechanisms applicable to judges. If the latter interpretation were adopted, the proposition would fail, he said. “As I understood the parties and both the sides kept in mind the higher judicial service only, that is High Court and Supreme Court judges. items.title: At BRICS PM Modi reiterates call for ‘dialogue and diplomacy’ in talks with Putin
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, September 11, once again told Russian President Vladimir Putin that “dialogue and diplomacy” were the way forward to resolve the conflict in Ukraine. The Prime Minister met his Russian counterpart on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, PM Modi said India remained willing to contribute to peace efforts. The two leaders also discussed the Ukraine war and the conflict in West Asia, including their impact on maritime trade. The conversation came shortly after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Kyiv, where he said the Ukraine conflict could only be resolved through dialogue, diplomacy and negotiations. India has maintained its engagement with Russia, including its purchases of Russian oil, despite growing pressure from the West. The safety of shipping in the Black Sea also figured in the Modi-Putin talks. India had raised concerns with both Moscow and Kyiv after attacks on merchant vessels in July killed Indian seafarers.
